claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Block duplication rose from 40.3 to 73.0 per million changed lines between 2023 and 2026 year-to-date, an 81% increase and the highest level on record.
claims.quote: Measured per million changed lines, block duplication climbed from 40.3 in 2023 to 73.0 year-to-date in 2026 — an 81% increase over 2023 and the highest level on record.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Moved/refactored code fell from 21% in 2022 to 3.8% year-to-date in 2026, while copy/paste rose from 9.4% in 2022 to 15.7% in the first half of 2026.
claims.quote: After clocking in at 21% in 2022, the percentage of moved code dropped to 13% of changed lines in 2023, before freefalling to 3.8% year-to-date in 2026. Over the same window, copy/paste climbed from 9.4% (in 2022) to 15.7% in the first half of 2026.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Function connectivity fell 35% since 2023, from 343 method calls per thousand changed lines to 223 year-to-date.
claims.quote: Function connectivity — how often newly authored code connects to a different method or function — has fallen 35% since 2023, from 343 method calls per thousand changed lines to 223 year-to-date.

claims.question: q5
claims.claim: Long-term update percent fell 74%, from 1.7% in 2023 to 0.46% year-to-date in 2026.
claims.quote: "Long-term update percent" — the share of changes that remove or update code last touched more than twelve months ago — has fallen 74%, from 1.7% in 2023 to 0.46% year-to-date in 2026.

claims.question: q6
claims.claim: The source states that throughput is real but so is the accrued debt, which concentrates among developers who have not recognized the failure modes threatening long-term maintainability.
